description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of sample counts across six distinct reasoning categories as part of the SRPO framework’s evaluation in enhancing multimodal LLM reasoning via reflection-aware reinforcement learning. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of Samples,” is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10² to 10⁴, with major gridlines at 100, 1,000, and 10,000. The horizontal axis lists the reasoning categories: “Mathematical Reasoning,” “General Reasoning,” “Natural Scene Reasoning,” “Visual Reasoning,” “Puzzle Reasoning,” and “Chemical Reasoning,” arranged in descending order of sample count. Each bar is rendered in light blue with its exact value labeled above: Mathematical Reasoning has 7,025 samples (tallest bar), General Reasoning has 1,709, Natural Scene Reasoning has 413, Visual Reasoning has 232, Puzzle Reasoning has 91, and Chemical Reasoning has 49 (shortest bar). The chart visually emphasizes the heavy skew toward Mathematical Reasoning, with sample counts decreasing sharply across subsequent categories, suggesting a focus or abundance of training or evaluation data in more abstract, formal reasoning domains compared to specialized or less common ones like Chemical Reasoning. A gray rectangular overlay partially obscures the label for “Visual Reasoning,” but its value remains legible.
